correctness.rationale: Directly differentiating the cited drifted mean produces the stationarity function B(s). Its derivative has a single sign transition, and B is positive at small positive s and negative at large s; thus exactly one transverse global optimum exists. At the optimum, the reactivity derivative vanishes exactly when a two-coefficient pencil has a common zero. That condition forces the inward relation m=u sqrt((u-1)/(u+1)) and one strictly decreasing scalar equation with exactly one root. The sign on the low-drift side is fixed by the exact B(1)=e/2-1>0 at zero drift. The high inward-drift sign is fixed at m=1 by the eta-downarrow-zero limit and propagated by continuity because no other zero is possible. The critical optimum is stationary for every finite eta, hence globally optimal by uniqueness. The packaged standard-library checker passed 534 finite tests; no finite test is used to certify the all-parameter result. The theorem requires only D,L,k>0 and arbitrary real mu; the singular k endpoints are not included.

value.rationale: The natural fixed-drift chemical control question—whether increasing point-trap reactivity should raise or lower the optimal Poisson reset frequency—is not resolved by the known mean formula or driftless result alone. The proof gives a sharp global parameter classification and an isolated rate invariant under arbitrary positive reactivity changes. This marks a qualitative reversal in the optimal kinetic-design response and a nontrivial boundary between transport-limited and reaction-limited restarting. It is a structural, motivated all-parameter theorem rather than an arbitrary computed slice or tiny numerical improvement; robustness to noisy drift estimation is explicitly outside its scope.
